title: Anorganic Bovine Bone vs. Biphasic Calcium Phosphate in a Large Series of Maxillary Sinus Floor Elevations-A Non-Randomized Clinico-Morphological Study
authors: Flichy-Fernández, A. J., Padial-Molina, M., Martin-Morales, N., Alegre-Domingo, T., Peñarrocha- Diago, M., O'Valle, F., & Galindo-Moreno, P. (2025). Anorganic Bovine Bone vs. Biphasic Calcium Phosphate in a Large Series of Maxillary Sinus Floor Elevations-A Non-Randomized Clinico- Morphological Study. Journal of clinical medicine, 14(23), 8464.
supports: Clinical study from the botiss Jason membrane (porcine pericardium) literature list — the product featured in it, which is not the same as the study being about the product, so check the design and the comparator before citing it as product evidence. Authors' conclusion, verbatim: “Although both biomaterials induce a similar amount of bone formation, the histopathological characteristics of the grafts are different, with a greater proportion of scar connective tissue with the biphasic calcium phosphate biomaterial” This records what the paper says, not what a rep may say: the sales wording still has to pass the claim tiers, and a study in one indication licenses nothing in another.
